Home dashboard

100-Acre Wood

Task allocation

OwnerTasksShare

Shared tasks count once for each assigned owner; "Everyone" tasks count for all five, and "Each child" tasks for each of the three kids. Percentages show the share of owner assignments, not time or effort. Open tasks are included; removed tasks are excluded.

Chores done

0chores done

Last 7 days

Counts chores marked done on the Calendar, on the day they were marked. Mark chores done with the round check on each one.

Tasks by owner

New owners override original assignments. Shared tasks appear under each owner, "Everyone" tasks under all five people and "Each child" tasks under each kid; tasks marked assignable that have no new owner yet appear under Open — needs an owner. Removed tasks are excluded.

Chores

Assignments

Everyone with their chores, and the parking lot of chores waiting for an owner. Tap a chore, then tap a name. Chores sit under their new owner, or the catalog owner if none is set, the same as Tasks by owner. The parking lot holds chores marked assignable that have no new owner yet.

When things happen

Calendar

Chores are spread across the days so nobody gets a pile-up. Drag a chore to another day, or tap it for details. Tap a day or month to zoom in; in the week view, tap a day's name to see just that day. Paid chores have a blue edge.

Standing Items

Done when they need doing, not on a set day. Tap the round check when one's done; each shows when it was last done.

Expectations, not to-dos

Soft skills

The way we work together. A task whose notes include #softskill or say it should be a soft skill shows up here too.

Admin

Users

Everyone who can sign in. Admins see every tab and everyone's data; everyone else sees only their own chores, soft skills and awards. To see the app exactly as someone else does, use Simulate user at the top.

One-off recognition

Awards

For the good stuff nobody can be assigned: cleaning up a mess you didn't make, pitching in without being asked. Tap a name to give the award.

Family & home needs

Maturity Marks

What growing up in this house looks like: the things to own without being asked. Where part of it is a chore, the card says so.
